title: China’s tech giants double AI spending to $139bn as labs earn less than 8%
content:
China’s AI companies face a money problem as well as a chip shortage, The New York Times’ Sui-Lee Wee and Li You reported on Friday. China’s biggest tech firms will double their AI spending this year. Their AI labs bring in a fraction of it.
The figures come from a Rhodium Group report on China’s AI financing, published in September. Rhodium surveyed 13 listed Chinese firms. It expects their AI infrastructure capex to rise 103% this year, to 932bn yuan ($139bn). It forecasts more than 1.2tn yuan ($193bn) in 2027. Revenue from their AI labs covers less than 8% of this year’s spend, according to Rhodium.
“When you look at their numbers, it looks like they’re running on a treadmill that’s speeding up and getting harder to run,” Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution, told the Times.
Money, not just chips
Most of the debate over China’s AI race has been about US export curbs on advanced chips. Washington moved this week to close one workaround, renting overseas data centres full of Nvidia hardware. Logan Wright, the Rhodium partner who co-wrote the report, sees a bigger hurdle. Financing constraints “will be probably more decisive” in the long run, he told the Times.
Rhodium puts China’s AI build-out at only 15% to 20% of the US level. The annual recurring revenue of all of China’s AI models was about $10.7bn, it found. That is roughly a tenth of what OpenAI and Anthropic report between them.
Alibaba, Baidu and Tencent, which back several of China’s top labs, now have negative cash flows, the Times reported. Tencent and Alibaba already warned this week that the new US curbs will slow growth in AI.
Investors have cooled too. China’s STAR 50 index, its answer to the Nasdaq, has fallen 43% since late July, the Times reported.
Open models, thin margins
China’s bet on open-source models has made the gap harder to close. Z.ai released GLM-5.3 Flash in August and halved its prices for two weeks. It wanted users to run the model on its own servers. By November, about 20 rival providers charged less than Z.ai for its own model, the Times reported, citing OpenRouter data.
Compute is scarce and expensive. On Goofish, a Chinese second-hand marketplace, sellers have listed Nvidia’s DGX B300 server for nearly $3m. That is about eight times the US price, the Times found.
DeepSeek’s chief executive, Liang Wenfeng, said Huawei’s chips are only about two years behind Nvidia’s. But DeepSeek would need four Huawei 950 chips to match one Nvidia GB300, he said. The Times cited a leaked transcript of his call with investors.
“We simply can’t afford to train the largest models available right now,” Liang said. DeepSeek did not respond to the Times’ request for comment.
Fewer places to raise
DeepSeek has raised more than $20bn, the Times reported, including a $15bn round backed by Tencent and CATL. Few rivals have such deep pockets.
Private AI investment in China reached $12.4bn in 2025, against $285.9bn in the US, according to Stanford’s AI Index. The index notes that this likely understates China’s total, because state guidance funds also pour money into AI. Foreign money has dried up, partly because Washington bars US venture capital from some Chinese technologies, the Times reported.
China still has strengths. Its researchers have repeatedly found ways to train and run models more cheaply. Han Lin, China country director at the Asia Group, told the Times the country has exceptional engineering talent and a government that can mobilise huge resources. What frontier technology also needs, he said, is risk capital that can absorb failure.

report.summary: 中国AI资本开支翻倍至1390亿美元，但AI实验室收入不足支出的8%
report.background: 围绕中国AI竞赛的讨论长期集中在芯片上——美国出口管制、海外租算力等。但Rhodium Group九月报告对13家中国上市公司的调研显示，真正的长期瓶颈可能是钱：这些公司今年AI基础设施资本开支预计增长103%至9320亿元人民币（约1390亿美元），2027年超1.2万亿元，而旗下AI实验室收入只能覆盖不到8%。同期阿里、百度、腾讯现金流已转负，投资人降温，科创50指数自7月底跌43%。中国AI建设规模目前仅为美国的15%至20%，全行业模型年度经常性收入约107亿美元，约为OpenAI与Anthropic合计的十分之一。
key_points: 投入与回报严重错位：13家上市公司AI资本开支今年翻倍至1390亿美元，自家AI实验室收入却覆盖不到8%，被形容为“在加速的跑步机上奔跑”。
融资比芯片更致命：Rhodium合伙人认为长期看资金约束比出口管制更具决定性。中国2025年私募AI投资124亿美元，美国为2859亿美元，外资还在撤离。
开源换市场、利润极薄：智谱GLM-5.3 Flash降价一半促销，两个月内约20家同行报价更低，模型能力难以转化为定价权。
算力贵得离谱：二手平台闲鱼上英伟达DGX B300标价近300万美元，约为美国价格8倍；DeepSeek梁文锋称4颗华为950才抵1颗GB300。
巨头现金流转负、股市转冷：阿里、百度、腾讯均出现负现金流，腾讯和阿里已预警美国新管制将拖慢AI增长，科创50自7月底跌43%。
report.impact: 对行业而言，中国AI可能走向“能力不落后太多、商业化严重滞后”的路径，价格战与开源策略会进一步压缩全球模型毛利，并让算力成为分层门槛。对开发者，低价甚至免费的高质量开源模型仍是红利，但API供应商稳定性、长期服务和生态支持需谨慎评估。对普通用户，短期内AI服务价格会继续走低、选择更多，但免费补贴难以长期持续，未来可能转向限速、会员或广告模式；同时国产算力适配会影响产品体验迭代速度。
report.tools: 想跟进可关注：DeepSeek、智谱GLM系列、Qwen等开源模型，用OpenRouter横向比价与调用；自建推理可看vLLM、SGLang并评估昇腾/CANN生态；数据侧可读Rhodium Group中国AI融资报告与斯坦福AI Index，跟踪资本开支与收入缺口变化。
